At first, Nina found it difficult to keep the habit. The experience taught Nina more than any book could. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The reading list grew to forty titles.
What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Nina thanked Ben for the honest advice. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. In fact, buses take contactless only.

Nina's dream job is to be a engineer. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. The reading room has become an important part of daily life. Dad was chuffed with the birthday card we made.

Nina wrote down every idea in a small notebook. The teachers' office looked quieter than usual that evening. Little by little, things began to change. Best of all, grandpa naps on the davenport every afternoon after lunch.
Nina ordered soup and tea at the reading room last night. There are always more possibilities than we expect. Nina is saving money to buy a ticket to London.
